waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

Which authoritative currency catalogue and maintaining authority governs the code used in this declaration?
Which published edition or snapshot of that catalogue was in force when this declaration was made?
Which list within the catalogue supplied the entry: current currencies and funds, registered fund codes, or historic entries?
How is the retained catalogue snapshot verified as unaltered before any code is resolved against it?
What must a consumer do when its own currency register differs from the catalogue named in this declaration?
Which alphabetic code and which numeric code identify the currency, and which form is authoritative for exchange here?
What constraints govern an accepted code token: character set, length, case and permitted normalization?
Is any presented currency symbol or localized name recorded strictly as a display label rather than as an identifier?
How are the alphabetic and numeric forms reconciled when the host supplies only one of them?
Which class does the code belong to: active national currency, registered fund code, precious metal, testing code, or no-currency code?
Is the code active or withdrawn according to the pinned catalogue edition rather than according to the current one?
Which minor-unit value does the catalogue publish for this code, and what happens when it is published as not applicable?
How is a code absent from the pinned catalogue edition recorded without silently defaulting to any currency?
What is explicitly not derivable from a currency code, and where is that prohibition recorded?
Which successor code does the catalogue associate with the withdrawn code used by this declaration?
What withdrawal or changeover period does the catalogue publish, and at what granularity is it published?
Which body declared the replacement or redenomination, and where is that declaration recorded?
Why must a historical amount stay expressed in its original currency inside this declaration rather than be restated in the successor currency?
What sign, integer coefficient and scale together represent the declared amount exactly?
Which exact encodings are permitted for the amount, and why is binary floating point excluded from them?
What total-digit and fraction-digit bounds does the host or profile impose on this amount?
How is a supplied value rejected when it cannot be held exactly at the declared scale?
What is the canonical lexical form of this amount, and how does it differ from any string rendered for display?
Are trailing zeros significant here, so that a value written with two fraction digits differs from the same value written with one?
How are zero and a signed negative zero distinguished, normalized or rejected in this declaration?
Which round-trip check proves that parsing and re-serializing preserves sign, coefficient and scale?
Which fields make up the indivisible declaration, and may any of them be stored or transmitted without the others?
Which host object and field declares this monetary value, and what meaning does the host assign to it?
What does a negative amount signify in this host context, and which signs are permitted at all?
How is the binding preserved when a target format splits amount and currency into separate fields?
Which determinacy state does this declaration assert: exact point value, interval, approximate value, unknown, missing or not applicable?
Which rule forbids expressing an absent, unknown or not-applicable monetary value as zero?
When an interval is declared, which endpoints are present and is each endpoint inclusive or exclusive?
How is an interval checked for a shared currency reference and a consistent scale across both endpoints?
What must a consumer do when it cannot honour a declared approximate or absent state?
What does the declared scale of this monetary amount assert about the meaningfulness of its digits?
How is a mismatch between the digits observed in a representation and the declared scale detected and reported?
Are numerically equal values with different exponents, such as 1 and 1.00, preserved as distinct declarations or normalised?
Which external accuracy attribute does this declaration map to when the value is exchanged?
Which published currency list and version supplied the minor-unit value used for this amount?
How is an amount handled when the currency has no defined minor unit or the code denotes a fund, metal or index?
What happens to previously recorded amounts when a currency's minor unit changes or the currency is withdrawn?
Where an exchange profile's decimal limit differs from the currency minor unit, which limit governs and how is the difference recorded?
Which named rounding mode applies to this value, and what authority establishes it?
Is the quantization target a power-of-ten scale or a non-decimal increment, and what exactly is that target?
How are exact half-way values resolved, and does the resolution differ by sign?
Which payment or presentation channel does this quantization rule apply to, and which channels does it explicitly exclude?
How is a change to the quantization rule versioned so that historic amounts remain reproducible?
Which precision tiers are declared for this value, and what scale does each tier carry?
At which points in the calculation was rounding applied, and was any intermediate result rounded?
When a value is derived by conversion, what precision governs the conversion factor and the intermediate result?
What is reported when a consumer requires a precision tier the producer did not declare?
Is this amount asserted as exact, rounded, truncated or estimated within bounds?
If the value is bounded rather than point-valued, what are the bounds and how were they derived?
Which operation introduced the inexactness, and was that recorded at the time the operation ran?
How does exactness status propagate when this amount is combined with other amounts?
What total-digit and fraction-digit capacity governs this value, and where does that limit originate?
Which arithmetic exception conditions must be surfaced to the host, and by what names?
What behaviours are prohibited when a value cannot be represented at the required scale?
How is decimal fidelity preserved when the value crosses a representation boundary?
Which attributes must match before two monetary values may be compared or added?
Does equality compare numeric value only, or numeric value together with scale and exponent?
What tolerance or materiality threshold applies to this comparison or reconciliation, and who set it?
What is returned when values are incompatible, and what must never happen implicitly?
Under which single rounding and valuation context is an aggregate reported, and how is that context recorded with the result?
Which allocation rule distributes the total, and how are the quantized parts derived from it?
Where is the residual assigned, and is it disclosed as an amount in its own right?
What evidence demonstrates that the allocated parts reconcile exactly to the total?
Is the allocation reproducible from the recorded inputs alone?
Which amount role does this monetary value carry, and from which classifier scheme and version is that role value drawn?
What identifier distinguishes this amount instance from the other role-tagged amounts derived from the same underlying value?
Which amount is the authoritative original that this role-tagged amount was derived from, and is that original still retrievable unchanged?
Which combinations of amount role and currency are prohibited or mandatory for this subject class?
What is the valuation instant, expressed with seconds and an explicit offset, at which this amount is asserted to hold?
When was this value observed or derived, and when was it ingested into the adopting store?
Is the valuation point an instant, the closing point of a reporting period, or an interval, and how is that distinction encoded?
What is recorded when the valuation point cannot be determined more precisely than a calendar date?
Which measurement basis is asserted for this amount, and which external standard or internal policy defines that basis?
Which body or policy owner is entitled to designate the measurement basis for this subject, and when was that designation made?
Which market, venue, trading session or scenario does the valuation refer to?
How is the valuation recorded when the currency is not exchangeable into the target currency at the valuation instant?
Which currency is base and which is quote for this quotation, and how many base units does the rate value price?
What is the rate value and to how many decimal places is it accurate as published?
Is the stored rate held in the publisher's direction or as an inverted value, and how is inversion flagged?
How does the stored direction map to a consumer or publisher whose quotation convention is the opposite?
Which named publisher or administrator produced this rate, and under which published methodology identifier?
What rate type is asserted, drawn from which pinned rate-type code list and version?
Is this source designated as authoritative for this subject class, and by whose decision was it admitted?
Which series or observation key in the owning publication model does this rate reference resolve to?
Over which effective or as-of interval is the referenced rate valid for this valuation?
What quality status does the rate carry at the moment it is bound to this valuation?
What staleness tolerance was applied when this rate was accepted, and who set that tolerance?
When was the rate published by its source and when was it retrieved by the adopting system?
Is the applied rate direct, inverse, cross or triangulated?
Which ordered constituent rates and pivot currencies make up the chain used to reach the target currency?
At which steps of the chain is intermediate rounding permitted, and at which is it prohibited?
How is the derived chain result checked against an independently published direct quotation when one exists?
Which exact equation, including multiplication or division direction, produced the converted amount?
In which order were conversion, chaining and rounding applied?
To which minor unit or decimal precision was the converted amount rounded, and under which rounding mode?
What residual difference between a recomputation and the stored value is tolerated before the record is flagged?
Which original amount does this converted amount derive from, and is that original preserved unchanged?
Which fee, spread, mark-up or tax components are referenced alongside this conversion, and in which model do they live?
Which amount is designated as the reported value when the original and converted amounts diverge?
What prevents a mark-up or spread from being absorbed into the recorded exchange rate?
Which minimum set of references and parameters must be retained for an independent party to recompute this converted amount?
How is a recomputation confirmed to reproduce the stored converted amount at the declared precision?
What captures the exact response received from the rate source at retrieval time?
Who may read the reproduction package, and which parts are withheld when the source licence limits redistribution?
Through which states does a valuation assertion move from asserted to superseded or withdrawn?
What triggers a correction — a revised source rate, a wrong classifier binding, or a rounding defect?
How long must a superseded assertion and its evidence remain retrievable, and under whose policy?
Who is accountable for issuing a correction and for informing downstream consumers of the superseded value?
Which party is recorded as accountable for this monetary value on its host record, and over what interval?
Which function stewards the currency code list and rounding configuration, and which body is named as the valuation authority for the basis applied?
Are preparer, independent reviewer and approver held by distinct parties for this assertion?
Under which declared rule may one party hold more than one of these positions, and what compensating declaration is then recorded?
What evidence supports each declared role assignment where the reviewer relied on an automated check rather than re-performance?
Which authority record permits a correction to the amount or currency of an existing monetary assertion?
On what basis was the exchange-rate source selected, and is the selection mandated by a jurisdictional rule or chosen under entity policy?
Which rounding and minor-unit policy version applies, and who is competent to change it?
What is recorded when the mandated rate source publishes nothing for the required instant or the currency is not exchangeable at the measurement date?
Which combination of host reference, role on the host, currency and valuation context uniquely identifies this monetary assertion?
Under which conditions must the adopting Dimension mint a surrogate identifier instead of relying on the host key?
How is this assertion distinguished from another that merely carries the same amount and the same currency?
Is the monetary assertion an inseparable component of the host record or a separately addressable record?
Which lifecycle states may a monetary assertion occupy on its host, and which transitions between them are permitted?
How are the interval over which the asserted value is effective and the instant at which it was recorded represented separately?
When a corrected amount is issued, is the prior assertion overwritten or retained as an immutable superseded version?
Which external record must be cited when the change is driven by an event this model does not own, such as a restatement or a re-issued source document?
Which ISO 4217 code-list edition and amendment number were in force when this currency code was resolved?
How does a value citing a withdrawn or replaced currency code remain interpretable after the register publishes the replacement?
Which policy versions - rounding, rate-source rule and accounting profile - are pinned to this assertion?
How is a pin recorded when the referenced register or policy publishes no version identifier?
From which original value, by which activity and with which applied rate was this derived monetary value produced?
Which agent is attributed responsibility for the derived value, and on whose behalf did that agent act?
Which instant does the applied rate refer to, and when was it retrieved from its publisher?
Is the recorded value an as-transacted amount, a translated amount or a re-measured amount?
What tolerance is accepted between a value recomputed from the lineage and the stored value?
Which integrity check value and algorithm are recorded for each evidence item supporting this value?
How is the completeness of the evidence set for a monetary assertion checked declaratively?
Which limitation must be stated when the supporting rate is published for information purposes only?
What is recorded when evidence is missing, superseded, or supplied by a party with an interest in the value?
Which external audit or assurance record is cited, and what does this model deliberately not assert about it?
Which sensitivity class applies, and does it attach to the amount, the currency, the counterparty or the derivation?
Which values are commercially restricted such that disclosure would breach a contractual confidentiality term?
Which resource and environment attributes must this model expose so that an external decision point can evaluate a request?
How is a required masked, banded or rounded projection of a restricted amount declared without asserting that masking has been applied?
Which time-bounded exceptions permit broader access, for example to a regulator or an external auditor?
Which retention class, trigger event and minimum period apply to this monetary context record and its evidence?
How is a legal hold recorded so that disposition is suppressed, and which external authority issued it?
Which end-of-life states may the record occupy, and which fields survive in a tombstone after disposal?
Which system executes disposal, and what does this model record as evidence that disposition occurred?
How are retention obligations reconciled when the host record and the monetary assertion carry different periods?
Which regional, tax or accounting profile governs this value, and which currency roles does it assign?
To which external representations is this monetary context mapped, and is each mapping an alignment or a claim of conformance?
Where the external representation cannot express a local field, what loss is declared and what round-trip behaviour is expected?
Which rule takes precedence when two profiles mandate different rate sources for the same underlying value?
Which checks must pass before a conformance claim, rather than an alignment, may be recorded?
Which effective instant and which observation cut-off instant does a read supply, and what is the declared default when either is omitted?
Which single assertion version is selected when more than one effective interval covers the requested instant, and how is a tie broken?
Which stored values must a read return verbatim, and which derivations are forbidden in the read path?
How does a read report an unresolvable host binding, a tombstoned assertion, or an as-of request outside the supported range?
Which resolvable identifier and attribute path anchor the assertion to its host, and how is that anchor demonstrated to resolve?
Which preconditions must hold before a create is accepted, and which of them are hard failures rather than warnings?
How is a repeated create recognised as the same request rather than as a second assertion?
Which outbound references must stay resolvable for the binding to remain valid, and what is reported when one of them breaks?
Which links connect a correcting version to the version it supersedes, and which agent and reason are recorded with it?
How is the effective interval of the superseded version closed, and how are gaps and overlaps across the version series detected?
Which concurrency validator must a correction present, and what happens when the validator is stale?
Which parts of a superseded version may never be rewritten, and how is an unusable version marked without erasing it?
Which evidence items must be present before a proposed monetary state change counts as reviewed?
Which authority is asserted to give the reviewer competence for this action, and where is that mandate recorded?
What does the eligibility report assert, and what does it explicitly decline to determine?
How is review evidence checked for currency and revocation before anyone relies on it?
Which holds or freezes currently suspend disposition of this assertion, and where does each one originate?
Which retention class or records schedule governs this assertion, and which authority owns that schedule?
What must remain after removal so that references from the host and from prior versions stay interpretable?
Which unresolved conditions block a readiness verdict, and how is an incomplete assessment expressed?
Which admissibility checks must a monetary value pass before any downstream calculation is attempted?
How is an unsupported, historic, fund or non-transactional currency identifier distinguished from an active transactional currency?
Which profile-specific constraints — allowed currency set, maximum total digits, maximum fraction digits and amount bounds — apply to the calling context?
What outcome is emitted when a value is inadmissible, and does that outcome block the operation or degrade it?
What rounding policy — target scale, rounding mode and tie-breaking rule — governs quantisation of this amount?
What residual arises from quantisation, and how is it computed, reported or allocated across components?
When may the target scale differ from the currency minor unit, and which authority pins that deviation?
How is precision loss detected and expressed so that a consumer knows the value is no longer exact?
Which rate source, publication and retrieval act produced the rate used for this derivation?
How are base and quote currencies, quotation direction and any intermediate leg expressed so the computation can be reproduced exactly?
Which reference time governs rate selection, and how does it differ from the valuation instant and the retrieval instant?
What arithmetic rules constrain the computation: multiplication versus division, permissibility of an inverse rate, intermediate scale and the order of quantisation?
What tolerance applies to this reconciliation, and is it derived from declared decimals, an absolute band or a relative band?
Which values form the reconciliation set, and on what basis are they comparable to each other?
What is emitted when the difference falls outside tolerance, and how is the unexplained residual attributed?
What must accompany a reconciliation result so that an independent party can recompute the same verdict?
Into which target representation is the value projected, and how are amount, currency and precision mapped without changing meaning?
Which redaction or generalisation operations are applied to the projected value, and which authorisation decision directed them?
How does the projection declare that it is lossy, non-reconcilable or partially suppressed?
How long may a projection be treated as current, and what marks it as superseded by a newer derivation?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
